en.title: Cyberpunk 2 Quest Team Half-Filled by Former Game Modders
en.summary: CD Projekt Red is tapping into the vibrant modding community for its highly anticipated sequel, Cyberpunk 2. Associate Game Director Pawel Sasko revealed that a significant portion of the quest design team comprises individuals who honed their skills by creating mods for the original game.
en.body:
The development of **Cyberpunk 2** is taking an interesting turn, with **CD Projekt Red** actively recruiting talent directly from the game's passionate modding community. In a recent REDstream discussion, **Pawel Sasko**, Associate Game Director for the sequel, shared that a remarkable half of the quest team working on **Cyberpunk 2** are former modders.

This revelation highlights a unique approach to game development, where the studio recognizes and cultivates the creativity that has kept **Cyberpunk 2077** alive and evolving long after its initial release. Sasko explained that for many of these individuals, modding served as a crucial "foot-in-the-door technique," providing invaluable experience in game design and development by allowing them to learn how things are built and customized within the game engine.

> "A lot of modders, they were players who actually first played and actually got experience with customizing the game with the mods. For me, this is a foot-in-the-door technique, and a gateway into game dev. You can see, and you can learn how things are made, how things can be built. We actually hired so many modders. I would say, at this point, half of the quest team is all former modders." — **Pawel Sasko**

## A Community Forged in Night City

This strategy is more than just a recruitment tactic; it's a testament to the enduring power of player creativity and the symbiotic relationship between developers and their communities. The modding scene for **Cyberpunk 2077** has been instrumental in adding new life to Night City, introducing innovative quests, visual enhancements, and gameplay tweaks that players have embraced. By bringing these talented individuals into the official development fold, **CD Projekt Red** is not only ensuring a deep understanding of player desires but also fostering a development environment that values grassroots innovation.

It’s a move that resonates deeply with fans who have invested countless hours into customizing their **Cyberpunk 2077** experience. Knowing that the very people who enhanced their game are now shaping its future sequel offers a unique sense of continuity and shared vision. This approach could lead to a **Cyberpunk 2** that feels even more attuned to the nuances and desires of its player base, building upon the lessons learned from both the original game's development and its vibrant modding ecosystem.

## The Road Ahead for Night City

While **Cyberpunk 2** is still a ways off, this insight into its development team offers a promising glimpse into what fans can expect. The focus on integrating experienced modders suggests a commitment to delivering a rich, detailed, and player-centric experience. Further details regarding **Cyberpunk 2**'s release date and specific gameplay features will be announced by **CD Projekt Red** in the coming months.

content_raw: Cyberpunk 2 associate game director Pawel Sasko revealed that a good chunk of the game’s staff are actually former modders who CD Projekt Red picked up to work on the highly-anticipated sequel. Sasko made these comments during one of CDPR’s REDstreams on October 21, where the team discussed the bevy of exciting new updates coming to Cyberpunk 2077 . As part of this discussion, they explained their decision to introduce cross-platform support for PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2, and Xbox Series X|S, saying this was done both to keep the game fresh and to actively support the creativity of its modders. In fact, the good folks at CDPR have actually partnered with modders in the game’s community as part of these updates, and even credited them with helping keep the title afloat. “The modding community is really keeping the game alive,” Sasko said. “I’m very often looking at what our modders are doing, what they’re building. It’s very exciting. There’s so much creativity. We as a studio always try to support our modding community as much as we can.” Adding onto this discussion, Sasko revealed that CDPR has sourced quite a few of its staff working on Cyberpunk 2 from the game’s modding scene, saying that around half of its quest team — designers who create a game’s objectives and storyline segments — are former modders. "A lot of modders, they were players who actually first played and actually got experience with customizing the game with the mods," he said. "For me, this is a foot-in-the-door technique, and a gateway into game dev," he continues. "You can see, and you can learn how things are made, how things can be built. We actually hired so many modders. I would say, at this point, half of the quest team is all former modders." While this isn’t a completely new revelation as far as CDPR is concerned (Sasko actually revealed this information back in 2024 ), it certainly couldn’t come at a funnier time, given the ongoing discussion around the differing sentiments toward community patches, mods, and emulation happening between Western players and Japanese fans on social media right now . It’s an exciting era for Cyberpunk chooms; Edgerunners 2 just released on Netflix to rave reviews, alongside a host of new additions to the actual game, which include a dual-wielding playstyle, fresh cyberware customization options, and even a mode that gives you a tour through Night City, on top of cute references to the anime spinoff.
